chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who swears an oath, then sees that leaving it is better, and if he does not leave it, he fears that he would sin. Should he leave it?
So he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the words of the Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family): 'Whenever you see something better than your oath, then leave it.'

key_terms.الْيَمِين: Oath (yamin) — a sworn commitment in the name of God; breaking an oath typically requires expiation (kaffara)
key_terms.تَرْكَهَا: Leaving/breaking the oath — permissible when a better alternative presents itself
key_terms.خَيْر: Good/better — the criterion for departing from an oath is finding a clearly superior option
key_terms.يَأْثَمَ: To sin/incur moral guilt — the fear of sin from fulfilling the oath justifies abandoning it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to break an oath if something better presents itself?
ai.summary: Sa'id al-A'raj posed a practical legal question to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): if a person swears an oath but later realizes that fulfilling it would lead to sin or that a better course of action exists, what should be done? The Imam answered by citing a well-known prophetic teaching — that the oath should be left when a better alternative is evident. This hadith reflects the flexibility inherent in Islamic jurisprudence regarding oaths, where expiation (kaffara) may be offered and the morally superior course pursued rather than rigidly adhering to a sworn commitment.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Al A’raj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who swore an oath, so he saw that leaving it is better, and if he were not to leave it, he fears that he would be sinning. Should he leave it?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Have you not heard the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Whenever you see (something) better than what you oathed for, so leave it’?’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sa‘id al-A‘raj who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who vows to do a certain thing then finds out that not doing it is better. If he disregards it, he is afraid of committing a sin. Can he disregard it?

He (the Imam) said, ‘Have you not heard the words of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, “If you find something better than that for which you have taken an oath, then you can disregard it.’””
